# GitHub protected-parent resolver (source preparation)

`github_parent.resolve_protected_parent(expectation_bytes, protected_facts, token, *, total_timeout=120)` resolves one fixed parent run in `forge-trust/AppSurface`. Inputs are the frozen `issue779-protected-parent-expectation-v1` bytes, a separate mapping containing exactly `workflow_path`, `workflow_sha`, `workflow_source_commit`, `base_sha`, and `subject_sha`, and an explicit GitHub API token argument. These facts must come from the caller's independently resolved protected source; workflow path/digest/base/subject must match the expectation, while `workflow_source_commit` is an additional immutable workflow commit pin. None are inferred from an uploaded document. The token is never read from an environment variable.

## Fixed request sequence

The resolver contacts only `https://api.github.com/repos/forge-trust/AppSurface/...` and constructs fixed endpoint paths itself:

1. `GET /actions/runs/{run_id}/attempts/{run_attempt}` requires the exact repository, run ID, attempt, candidate run-head SHA, supported event (`push` or `workflow_dispatch`), completed status, success conclusion, and actual workflow path carried by that run. A candidate head or branch is only an identity; the API repository/path does not establish that its workflow is protected.
2. `GET /contents/{workflow_path}?ref={workflow_source_commit}` reads bounded workflow content at the separate immutable commit supplied by the protected caller. The resolver recomputes Git blob SHA-1 from returned bytes, requires it to match GitHub's blob SHA, and matches the independent protected workflow digest (Git blob SHA-1 or raw-byte SHA-256).
3. `GET /contents/{workflow_path}?ref={run_head_sha}` independently fetches the workflow bytes at the actual run head. Those bytes must have the same protected digest and content as the protected workflow revision; a candidate run with a modified workflow is rejected before artifact listing or download. The run's `head_repository` and artifact's `workflow_run.head_repository_id` must identify the same protected repository as the run repository.
4. `GET /actions/runs/{run_id}/artifacts?per_page=100&page=N` uses finite pagination (at most 10 pages). It requires one exact artifact ID and matching name, workflow-run ID, repository ID, head repository ID and candidate head SHA, unexpired status, bounded size, and expected `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` digest.
5. `GET /actions/artifacts/{artifact_id}/zip` downloads only the selected artifact. The bearer token is sent only to `api.github.com`. Redirects are handled manually for at most three hops over HTTPS and limited to `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, `github-production-repository-file-*.s3.amazonaws.com`, and `*.blob.core.windows.net`; redirect destinations never receive the token. No URL, repository, or endpoint template comes from the caller.
6. The exact download is capped at 32 MiB and passed with separately serialized API projections to frozen `provenance.preflight_protected_parent`. That parser checks metadata digest, expected digest, and downloaded bytes before bounded ZIP parsing, then selects exactly `plan.json` and `manifest.json`.

The API token is sent on the fixed `api.github.com` requests only (run attempt, protected workflow content, actual run-head workflow content when distinct, artifact listing, and artifact ZIP endpoint); no authorization header is sent on redirected storage requests. The resolver allows at most 20 HTTP requests, 10 artifact-list pages, 1 MiB per API response, 15 seconds per request, and a 120 second default monotonic total deadline. It does not retry requests. JSON responses reject duplicate or case-aliased keys. Tests replace only the private `_open_request` function with detached in-memory fixtures; they make no GitHub requests and establish no real protected-parent proof.

Archive preflight consumes that same original monotonic allowance. A final deadline check after digest/ZIP/document processing rejects an expired result before returning `ProtectedParentResolution`; parsing does not renew the network budget.

## Trust boundary

The frozen `ProtectedParentResolution` returns selected document bytes plus run/artifact identifiers. It is not an authenticated-proof receipt, policy decision, admission, `Trusted` value, or gate result. Successful HTTP/API consistency does not authenticate the protected facts supplied by the caller. The eventual caller must independently source the expectation and facts, apply semantic checks to the selected documents, and invoke the existing gate only through its separately reviewed protected path. This resolver adds no workflow, registration, runtime capability, admission mechanism, or positive acceptance claim. Real API integration, caller wiring, semantic-gate review, and protected execution remain pending.

Importing the module performs no network request, token lookup, process launch, or filesystem write. No command-line interface is provided.
